critic_notes.rationale: Internally consistent and coherently signed, but it is essentially a two-leg quality composite (operating profitability × low cash-flow volatility) that closely tracks published QMJ/"safety-adjusted profitability" constructions, so it is acceptable as a generation-0 baseline rather than a novel interaction.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the sign is correct, though "profitability improvement validated by low accruals" is a well-trodden combination of the accruals anomaly with fundamental-momentum, and the rank product means firms with deteriorating profitability *and* low accruals are also pushed to the short leg, which slightly muddies attribution.

Dividing an industry-demeaned (sign-changing) gross-profitability measure by lt/at is not monotone in either leg — low-liability firms with below-industry profitability get extreme negative scores while high-liability firms with the same profitability get near-zero scores — so the signal does not implement the stated "profitability premium is stronger with light liabilities" hypothesis and 1% winsorization will not repair the small-denominator instability.

This stacks three separately published quality effects (net profitability, retained-earnings-to-assets, earnings volatility) into a single product-of-ranks, so any result is uninterpretable as an interaction and largely rediscovers known profitability/retained-earnings anomalies.

The construction genuinely isolates the "profit spike unsupported by cash" corner and the negative expected sign follows naturally from the expression, though it is close to the established result that the accruals anomaly is concentrated among firms with large earnings increases, and the rank-product also assigns low scores to sharply deteriorating high-accrual firms, which weakens the short leg's purity.

The hard 0/1 gate collapses roughly half the cross-section (all firms that increased liability intensity) to an identical value of zero regardless of profitability, producing a degenerate, mechanically unstable short leg whose spread will mostly reflect the known leverage-change/debt-issuance effect rather than the claimed profitability-conditional-on-deleveraging interaction; it is also largely redundant with the first proposal's profitability leg.

This is structurally the archived "Debt-Light EBITDA Strength" with cosmetic substitutions (operating surplus for EBITDA, total liabilities for debt, industry-adjustment, no smoothing), and profitability-times-low-leverage is itself the standard QMJ/Piotroski quality composite rather than a new mechanism.

Same rank(profitability) × rank(low leverage) template as the archived signal, with the interest-expense term adding little independent information since xint/at is largely a mechanical function of the debt/at term already in the SUMRANK.

The profitability leg is essentially identical to the archived signal's (oibdp ≈ ebitda, same 3-period MA) but the current-ratio quality leg is a genuinely different balance-sheet dimension; the concern is that high current ratios often flag bloated inventory/receivables and idle assets, so the expected positive sign on that leg is not obviously right.

The expression is internally consistent with the stated negative sign and the "turnaround trap" framing is a real interaction hypothesis, but any negative slope will be hard to attribute to the interaction because low retained-earnings/assets is a standalone distress proxy with its own documented negative return relation.

The second leg (Δdebt/at plus Δinterest/at) is effectively net debt issuance, a well-documented external-financing anomaly with a strong negative main effect, so a negative slope would almost certainly be a rediscovery rather than evidence for the profit-acceleration interaction.

The construction is sound (the |m| term makes it a bounded monotone transform of signed profitability-to-instability, so no sign pathology) and the current-liability volatility term is a real cross-theme addition, though the core profitability/earnings-volatility ratio is close to the known earnings-smoothness and profit-persistence literature.

This is a cosmetic swap of the second leg in the archived "Liquidity-Backed Operating Yield" (act/lct → oancf/lct) with an identical profitability leg, and the new leg is itself highly correlated with the profitability leg (oancf ≈ oibdp scaled), so it double-counts rather than adding an independent conditioning dimension.

Liability maturity mix (lct/lt) is a genuinely distinct conditioning variable from the archived total-debt-intensity and current-ratio legs, though it reuses the same rank-product template and carries a latent tension — low current-liability share often means *more* long-term debt, which cuts against the earlier debt-light result and should be diagnosed if the sign disappoints.

The contrast with the archived liquidity-cushion result is well motivated, but the second leg is essentially current-asset turnover — a known DuPont/asset-turnover anomaly component that is also mechanically a factor of the profitability leg itself (oibdp/at = margin × turnover) — so any success may be a rediscovery rather than a true interaction.

TS_RANK of re/at over a 5-period window is near-degenerate for the typical firm (RE/AT drifts monotonically upward for any profitable firm, pinning the rank at its maximum and creating massive ties), so the second leg mostly re-expresses profitability rather than providing the independent "quality backing" the hypothesis claims.

The dominant driver of the second leg is (ib − oancf)/at, i.e. the Sloan accrual anomaly, and the overall construction is a close cousin of the archived "Cutback Liquidity Profit Accel Trap" (which already failed with a sign-contradicting fmb_tstat), so this is largely a repackaged known effect on a template that has not worked here.

R&D-added-back operating profitability is coherent (xrd sits inside SG&A/oibdp) and the bounded re/(|re|+lt) self-financing leg is a non-obvious construction that handles deficit firms gracefully, but both legs edge toward known anomalies (R&D-adjusted profitability, retained-earnings-to-value), so the incremental content over the archived RE-based signals needs to be demonstrated rather than assumed.

This is a leg-swap recombination of two archive signals (the residual cash-conversion quality leg from "Residual Cash Conversion Margin" and the profitability leg from "Liquidity-Backed Operating Yield"), and the quality leg is itself close to the published cash-based-operating-profitability/accruals anomaly, so the incremental information is mostly a coverage adjustment rather than a new mechanism.

The TS_MIN "worst-case coverage floor" is a genuinely new conditioning construct rather than another contemporaneous-level interaction, the sign direction matches the expression, and it plausibly separates durable from fragile profitability — though coverage should be checked given the five-period oancf history requirement.

It conjoins two already-tested archive legs, one of which (sale/act productivity) delivered a significantly negative FF5 alpha, and act/lct versus sale/act are partly mechanically opposed in act, so the MIN gate mostly selects on low lct and high sale rather than testing a coherent new "healthy working capital" mechanism.

The economic claim — profit-trend momentum validated by retained-capital backing — is essentially the already-failed "Retention-Backed Profit Momentum" (fmb 1.00, ls_talpha −0.27) with re level substituted for Δre and sales-scaling for asset-scaling, and both legs come directly from archive signals, making it a cosmetic variant.

Since dp is strictly positive and |oiadp| sits in the denominator, the second leg is monotonically decreasing in profitability and therefore largely double-counts leg one rather than acting as an independent conditioner; economically it also reduces to profitability × low capital intensity, a well-worn combination, and it is internally odd to penalize depreciation in a measure already net of depreciation.

Leverage-intensity *stability* is a substantively different conditioning mechanism from the archive's debt-*level* composite, the sign is coherent with the expression, and the recapitalization/financing-stress rationale is testable — though the result should be checked for collinearity with debt level and for coverage loss from the five-period VOL window.

This is a one-leg swap on the archive's "Liquid Profitability Floor" (same TS_MIN(oibdp/at) leg) where the replacement conditioner is the lct/sale intensity leg that already produced essentially zero alpha in "Current-Claim Clean Margin," so it reads as a cosmetic recombination unlikely to add information.

The x/(|x|+debt) construction is internally inconsistent because for loss-making firms (negative TS_MIN) higher debt makes the score *less* negative, reversing the intended penalty, and this exact denominator form already failed in "Operating Profit Reliability Ratio" while the simpler MUL version ("Debt-Light EBITDA Strength") already worked.

It stacks two constructions that already failed in the archive (fixed-charge coverage of current liabilities, and the signed x/(|x|+vol) normalizer with its sign-flip pathology for negative numerators) and additionally mismatches scaling by dividing an lct-scaled numerator against an at-scaled volatility term.

The intangible-adjusted profitability leg conditioned jointly on R&D commitment and liquidity is a defensible extension of the archive's promising fmb-but-weak-alpha R&D signal, though COALESCE(xrd,0) creates a large tied mass of non-R&D firms in the TREND leg and a rising R&D/sales trend arguably points the other way (investment/asset-growth anomaly), so the conditioning sign is not clearly justified.

TS_SUM(INDICATOR(oiadp/at,0),5) is nearly saturated and highly redundant with the MA profitability level, so the MIN gate collapses for most firms into NEG(VOL(lct/at)) — a leg already tested via "Stable Capital Structure Profit" and "Maintenance-Stable EBITDA Quality" with ~zero alpha.

It is a single-variable substitution (act→lct) on the archive's "Working-Capital Efficient Margin Expansion" rather than a substantive re-diagnosis of why that signal's alpha was insignificant, and the new leg's direction (falling current liabilities per sale) mechanically implies *higher* working-capital accruals, which conflicts with the well-known accrual anomaly's negative return prediction.

This is a pure operator swap (MIN for MUL) on the archive's "Liquidity-Backed Smooth Operating Profit" using identical legs — a cosmetic variant of an already-tested signal rather than a new mechanism.

It mechanically welds together two already-evaluated archive signals ("Liquid Net Operating Floor" and "Trough EBITDA Debt Ceiling") whose legs are highly correlated conditioners, so the marginal information over prior tests is minimal.

The accrual conditioner (ib − oancf)/at is literally the Sloan (1996) accruals measure and its interaction with profitability is the published cash-based operating profitability anomaly (Ball et al. 2016), and it also closely echoes the archive's "Residual Cash Conversion Margin."

The depreciation-conversion leg is a genuinely new and economically sensible way to discount EBITDA quality (though the |ebitda|+dp denominator is arbitrary and largely reduces to inverse depreciation intensity, overlapping "Hollow Levered EBITDA Trap"), and the recycled act/lct conditioner limits its incremental value.

TS_COUNT(xrd,5) is effectively a near-binary R&D-reporting dummy with massive rank ties, so under MIN the signal collapses to the already-tested profitability×current-ratio construct restricted to R&D reporters — a weak variant of "Liquid Sustained RND Profit."

Pairing an interest-adjusted profitability trend with a peak-leverage conditioner is a coherent and reasonably distinct construction (level-based floor versus trend), though both components are individually close to known profitability-growth and leverage effects and the archive's trend-based legs have generally produced weak alphas.

This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "Liquid EBITDA Conversion" (IND_ADJ→MA(3) on the profitability leg, contemporaneous conversion→TS_MIN(5) on the conversion leg), with both substitutions already shown elsewhere in the archive to move results only marginally, so it tests no new economic channel.

Mechanically it just swaps the act/lct leg of archived "Liquid EBITDA Conversion" for the NEG(TS_MAX(debt/at,5)) leg of archived "Trough EBITDA Debt Ceiling" and "Debt-Ceiling Net Profit Momentum," and since both conditioning legs already delivered near-identical ~3% alphas with t≈2.9-3.1, the recombination's outcome is largely pre-determined rather than informative.

TS_MIN(act/lct,5) is near-collinear with the plain current ratio already used in eight archived signals, and pairing it with the after-interest profit trend leg from "Debt-Ceiling Net Profit Momentum" yields a signal that sits between two existing entries without introducing a distinct mechanism; the recurring act/lct leg also raises the concern that the liquidity/size dimension, not profitability quality, is driving the repeated ~4% alphas.

The gross-profit leg is essentially Novy-Marx gross profitability (a known anomaly) and the liquidity leg is heavily reused, but the overhead-absorption conversion ratio oiadp/(|gross profit|+xsga) is a genuinely new intermediate-margin quality measure not present in the archive, making this the most substantively novel proposal of the batch.

This is archived "Self-Funded RND Profit" with oancf replaced by act in the numerator and the R&D accumulation window shortened from 5 to 3 — a parameter/denominator tweak that also collapses toward the already heavily-tested current-ratio leg rather than a new economic hypothesis.

It bolts the MA-minus-VOL smoothness leg from "Liquidity-Backed Smooth Operating Profit" onto the debt-ceiling leg from "Trough EBITDA Debt Ceiling," so it is a two-component recombination of archived legs; the SUB(mean, volatility) construction is also scale-arbitrary (subtracting a standard deviation from a level with no scaling coefficient), making any result hard to interpret economically.

This is a near-clone of the archived "Liquid Gross Operating Conversion" (same gross-profitability leg, same act/lct conditioner) with only the conversion denominator swapped from xsga to lct, and that swap actually contradicts the stated hypothesis of testing whether gross surplus "survives overhead," since overhead no longer appears in the ratio.

It reuses the archived gross-to-operating conversion leg but replaces the recurring liquidity conditioner with a genuinely different fixed-charge-stability measure, making it a defensible (if leg-swap-style) test of whether the conversion mechanism survives without current-ratio conditioning.

The demand-stability conditioner (low asset-turnover volatility) is a new ingredient relative to the archive's overhead-, cash-, and claim-based margin conditioners and is internally consistent, though VOL(sale/at) conflates revenue instability with asset-base churn and the act/lct leg is heavily reused.

Profitability × low-debt-intensity has already been tested twice in the archive (Debt-Light EBITDA Strength, Liquidity-Backed Operating Yield), and narrowing the debt measure to dlc/act is a cosmetic denominator change rather than a new mechanism.

The base signal is identical to the archived Liquid Gross Operating Conversion and the substituted ceq/lt conditioner is essentially inverse book leverage, i.e., the same low-leverage-supports-profitability idea already covered by Debt-Light EBITDA Strength and Internally Funded RND Profit.

Replacing the archive's weak accrual-based gross-surplus-over-(xsga+lct) ratio with a cash-flow-funded coverage conditioner interacted with industry-adjusted gross profitability is a coherent and reasonably distinct construction, though oancf will cut coverage and the mechanism overlaps the earlier residual-cash-conversion theme.

This is a cosmetic re-scaling of the archive's best signal (Liquid Gross Operating Conversion), swapping act/lct for the monotonically related (act−lct)/at while leaving the other two legs identical, so it tests essentially the same construct rather than a new mechanism.

It is the fourth permutation of the same "IND_ADJ gross profit × gross-to-operating conversion × third quality filter" template already probed with liquidity (0.044/3.83), interest-burden stability (0.029/2.89) and sales-stability legs (Demand-Stable Liquid Margin), so the incremental information from substituting VOL(sale/act) is minimal and likely to load on the same spread.

The liability-mix leg reduces cleanly to (lct − dlc − dltt)/lt, which is a genuinely different economic decomposition (non-debt operating float vs. funded debt) and is motivated by an explicit diagnosis of why the earlier NEG(lct/lt) maturity-mix interaction produced a reliably wrong-signed alpha.

The construct is internally coherent, but it is structurally the same "hollow profitability trap" design as the archived Hollow Levered EBITDA Trap (which delivered contradictory fmb and alpha signs), and the expected negative sign is fragile because the dominant leg is high industry-adjusted gross profitability, whose known premium runs the other way.

This simply multiplies an archived profitability leg by the volatility of an archived cash-coverage ratio, ignoring that the closely related VOL(oancf/lct) stability leg already produced a significantly negative FF5 alpha (−0.025, t=−2.11) contradicting the assumed positive sign, and the 3-year VOL window makes the quality leg noisier still.

Stability of non-debt current liabilities scaled by COGS is a reasonably distinct quality construct not present in the archive and pairs sensibly with the conversion leg, though the conversion ratio alone is a recycled component and the mechanism overlaps with the companion operating-float proposal.

Adding depreciation (ebitda − oiadp) to a *liquidity* denominator is economically incoherent — a noncash charge is not a near-term claim — and because dp is small relative to lct the leg ranks nearly identically to act/lct, making this a cosmetic variant of the already-tested Liquidity-Backed Operating Yield / Liquid EBITDA Conversion signals.

It preserves the archive's strongest mechanism (industry-adjusted gross profitability × gross-to-operating conversion) while substituting a genuinely different conditioner — non-debt operating float versus funded debt share of total liabilities — rather than the generic current ratio, so the test is informative even though both legs are individually familiar.

This is a mechanical crossover of two existing archive legs (TS_MIN of after-interest profitability from Liquid Net Operating Floor and VOL of interest burden from Interest Burden Stable Profit), and the volatility leg degenerates toward a low/no-debt indicator (zero xint ⇒ zero volatility), so it largely re-tests the already-documented Debt-Light EBITDA / Trough EBITDA Debt Ceiling effect with redundant xint on both sides.

Conditioning gross-to-operating conversion on the recent *maximum* short-term-debt share of current liabilities is a defensible rollover-risk conditioner that is distinct from the previously tested volatility and float-stability versions, though the omission of the industry adjustment that helped related signals is a weakness given Stable Operating-Float Converter's sharply negative alpha.

Both legs are lifted verbatim from mediocre archive signals (Demand-Stable Net Operating Yield's VOL(sale/(at+lct)) and margin-floor variants), and it drops the IND_ADJ that was needed to make raw operating margin comparable across industries, so it reads as a downgraded recombination rather than a new mechanism.

Three-leg complexity built entirely from archive components, one of which (re/at − lct/at) already delivered ~zero/negative alpha in Retained Cushion Net Profit Floor, and the R&D treatment is internally inconsistent since xrd is added back in the numerator while xsga (which contains xrd) remains in the denominator.
